alignments.note: 'utterly cast down' taken as the ASV's whole rendering of the hophal of טול (hurled headlong); marking 'utterly' added was the competing reading.

יָדוֹ is the bare direct object of סוֹמֵךְ in the Hebrew; the ASV recasts it as an instrument and supplies 'with', which rule 33's direct-object paragraph sends to the verb's unit under rule 44 whatever preposition was chosen. Discontinuous around the supplied 'him' (rule 25). Giving 'with' to the noun under rule 33 was the competing reading. Margin 'upholdeth his hand' read and set aside (rule 38).
Supplied object 'him'; no object morpheme stands in the clause, the Hebrew object being 'his hand' (rule 44).
Noun keeps only its own word; the supplied 'with' is the verb's.

review_notes: Moved the supplied 'with' from יָד to סוֹמֵךְ: the noun is the verb's direct object in the Hebrew, so rule 33's direct-object paragraph hands the recast preposition to the verb under rule 44 rather than to the noun.
